title: refactor(ci): consolidate workflows, bump GitHub Actions, and clean up release automation
author: Ava Patel
description:
Motivation: our repository had many overlapping GitHub Actions workflows (separate lint/test/release flows per repo area), multiple hard-coded action versions, and duplicated caching logic. This PR consolidates CI workflows into a small set of reusable templates, bumps GH Actions versions (actions/checkout, setup-node, cache, upload-artifact) to current recommended releases, centralizes cache key logic, and simplifies the release automation to reduce flakes and maintenance burden.

What changed (high level): consolidates per-repo CI into unified reusable workflows, introduces .github/workflows/ci-reusable.yml for job templates, replaces several legacy workflow files with calls to the reusable workflow, standardizes Node versions matrix, updates cache keys to include lockfile/ci-metadata, upgrades action versions to address security warnings, and simplifies release.yml to avoid duplicate tagging steps.

Checklist:
- [x] Add reusable workflow templates and migrate lint/test jobs to call them
- [x] Bump GH Actions and action versions (checkout@v4, setup-node@v3, actions/cache@v4)
- [x] Centralize cache key and restore logic
- [x] Fix lint step to use eslint cache from workspace and aggressive parallelism guard
- [x] Validate release workflow on canary branch before main rollout
- [x] Run full monorepo CI in a staging run and green builds across core services

Testing and rollout: ran entire monorepo CI on branch (2026-02-20) with deterministic cache hits, all unit/integration tests passed across redwood, redwood-sdk-python and redwood-docs. Release workflow was tested on release/canary and validated end-to-end without creating a public tag. Rollout: merged to main after approvals and will be monitored for 72 hours for any new flakes.

Notes: this is a refactor only (no runtime code changes). We intentionally kept semantic behavior of test jobs unchanged; performance improvements come from reduced duplicated setup steps and better cache hit rates. If anything regresses, revert is straightforward by restoring replaced workflows from this branch.
commits: consolidate: introduce ci-reusable.yml (reusable workflow templates for lint/test/build)
chore(ci): replace legacy lint/test workflows with reusable workflow calls
fix(ci): standardize cache key to include lockfile and repo-identifier
chore(release): simplify release.yml to single-source-of-truth tagging step
chore(docs): update CONTRIBUTING.md CI section to reference new workflows
review_comments: Jun Park: Nice cleanup — can we keep the Node matrix to the exact runtimes we test daily instead of a wide matrix? Suggested using [16,18] only.
Ava Patel: Updated matrix to 16 and 18 to match supported runtimes. Left a comment why 20 is excluded (not pinned for production yet).
Miguel Ramirez: Observability comment — add step to emit workflow-run id and cache hit metric to CloudWatch/Datadog (we can iterate).
Ava Patel: Added a small step to echo WORKFLOW_RUN_ID and cache restore stat; will follow up with metrics ingest in a separate PR (ENG-4972).
Olivia Chen: release.yml change looks safer. One suggestion: gate release on a 'release-guard' env var so we can opt-out during emergency merges.
Ava Patel: Added release-guard input with default 'true' and documented usage in CONTRIBUTING.md.
release_notes: Refactor CI workflows: consolidated reusable workflow templates, upgraded GitHub Action versions for security and stability, centralized cache keys to improve cache hit rates, and simplified release automation. No runtime changes. Expect faster CI startup and fewer duplicated workflow maintenance tasks.
